summary: Best: val_bpb 0.982130 (commit 2dbf3ed) vs the 0.997359 baseline, on a stack of TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2^18 (a0), varlen document masking (a2), value embeddings on all 8 layers (mine), dim 640 (a0), WINDOW_PATTERN 'L' (mine), DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128 so grad_accum is 1 (mine), WARMDOWN_RATIO 1.0 and EMBEDDING_LR 0.4 (a2). What worked in my own lane: value embeddings on every layer instead of alternating layers is free (vocab is only 8192, so a table is 4.2M params and ~0 FLOPs/token) and was worth about -0.0006 alone and more in combination; dropping sliding windows entirely once varlen doc-masking is in is quality-neutral but cuts peak VRAM 45GB->29GB, and spending that headroom on device batch 128 (grad_accum 2->1) was worth about -0.0009. What did not work, all measured: gated ReLU^2 MLP (+0.0074), U-net encoder/decoder skips (+0.0095, probably redundant with the existing x0_lambdas input skip), HEAD_DIM 64 (+0.011) and 256 (+0.012) around the 128 optimum, MLP expansion 2x (+0.022) and 5x (+0.0023) around the 4x optimum, and shortening the window to 256 (neutral). The shape of this model is a genuine local optimum; only free-capacity and step-count changes moved the needle. Next I would sweep TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE again on top of the final stack (2^18 was tuned before varlen, VE-all and dim 640 existed, so the optimum has probably moved), try a short LR warmup now that grad_accum is 1, and retune MATRIX_LR jointly with the new batch size.
